data.markdown:
_Account POV. Drawing the org and overlaying our engagement._

Pulling internal data for CoreFlow.

Open opportunity: CoreFlow - Enterprise 2026, stage negotiation, $142K, close date 2026-09-11 (SFDC).

Engagement is concentrated in the Lifecycle Marketing function. Chris Jones (Head of Lifecycle Marketing, flagged as champion, recently hired per org data) has appeared on all three recorded calls: Discovery (2026-06-17), Pricing Review (2026-06-22), and QBR (2026-06-24). Nicole Anderson, Stephanie Clark, and Daniel Davis also joined individual calls. Robert Smith (CMO) appeared on the Discovery call and sits one level above Jones in the org, reporting to CEO Margaret Chen. No contact from Engineering (Victor Osei, Tom Bradley) or Finance (Priya Raman, VP Finance) has appeared on any call.

Priya Raman's enrichment confidence is 0.55 and Tom Bradley's is 0.45, so both rows are worth verifying before treating them as reliable.

Two contacts carry the same title, Head of Lifecycle Marketing: Chris Jones and Daniel Davis. The data does not clarify whether these are parallel roles, a data duplication, or a hierarchy gap. Worth confirming.

An open Director of Lifecycle Marketing role is listed in the org (confidence 0.80), posted 2026-07-24 on LinkedIn. A separate Head of Lifecycle Marketing posting appeared 2026-06-30 and again 2026-07-04 (linkedin.com/jobs/view/29c03ea7 and linkedin.com/jobs/view/3fb10b41). The active buildout of the comp team may indicate the function is being expanded under the new round.

The funding signal data contains some inconsistency: one signal dated 2026-07-28 cites a $100M Series C led by Accel, while another dated 2026-07-30 cites a $15M Series C led by a16z, and a third dated 2026-07-01 describes a $100M Series B led by Bessemer (crunchbase.com/organization/corepay/funding_rounds). These three signals conflict on round size, round label, and lead investor. The true funding picture is unresolved from this data alone.

No rows returned from the Engagement adapter, so email-level contact data is not available here.

data.markdown:
_Scanning your accounts._

Every account in the data has an open opportunity in Salesforce, so the outbound filter is not the issue here. The signal scanner surfaces active buying signals across the book regardless of opp stage; it is the outbound rule that blocks open-opp accounts from cold-prospect lists. Below are the five accounts with the most active signals in the last 45 days, ranked by recency and count.

CoreFlow (finance, 1,531 employees, open opp: negotiation, close 2026-09-11)
Two funding signals in three days: $100M Series C led by Accel detected 2026-07-28 (crunchbase.com/organization/corepay/funding_rounds) and a second $15M Series C signal led by a16z detected 2026-07-30 (same source). The data shows two separate signals for what may be the same round reported across sources, worth confirming. A raise of that size at negotiation stage likely raises board attention on talent-strategy spend and headcount planning.

NovaGrid (manufacturing, 2,025 employees, open opp: qualification, close 2026-12-03)
Two signals across four days. $5M Series C led by a16z detected 2026-07-29 (crunchbase.com/organization/novacomp/funding_rounds). Case-studies page revisited four times in the last seven days, third visit this week detected 2026-08-01, session duration 247 seconds (gtm-os.internal/analytics/sessions/271bd402-14e). A contact spending that much time on case studies may be building an internal business case, though no source confirms who the visitor is.

PeakPoint (healthcare, 15,355 employees, open opp: proposal, close 2026-10-30)
Pricing page revisited five times in the last seven days, third visit detected 2026-07-29, session duration 547 seconds (gtm-os.internal/analytics/sessions/45825d84-e9b). Repeated, extended pricing-page visits at proposal stage may indicate active internal cost review. Largest account in the signal set by employee count.

PeakForce (healthcare, 2,015 employees, open opps: prospecting and negotiation, negotiation close 2026-09-04)
Pricing page revisited five times in the last seven days, third visit detected 2026-07-28, session duration 110 seconds (gtm-os.internal/analytics/sessions/6ebcaf3c-a88). Renewal opp is in negotiation with a close date less than a month out, so the pricing-page activity sits against an active renewal conversation.

FuseWorks (manufacturing, 531 employees, open opp: prospecting, close 2027-01-24)
Two signals across seven days. $30M Seed round led by Accel detected 2026-07-25 (crunchbase.com/organization/fuseworks/funding_rounds). A $30M Seed is unusually large, so board attention on hiring pace and comp structure is likely high. Director of Lifecycle Marketing opening posted on LinkedIn 2026-08-01 (linkedin.com/jobs/view/7c502eb0), located in Scotland. A first or senior comp hire at a freshly funded company typically begins band-building and benchmarking work in the first 90 days. No champion identified in the data.
